newsitem.title: USA: Seven muni groups challenge IRS yield burning plan.
newsitem.headline: Seven muni groups challenge IRS yield burning plan.

text.p: Seven state and local government groups said the IRS' controversial "yield burning" ruling should be revoked because it violates the U.S. Congress' recent curbs on unfunded mandates.

The $1.3 trillion municipal bond market has been rocked by allegations that bond underwriters overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond refinancing deals, a practice called yield burning.

The Internal Revenue Service's 1996 "closing agreement" plan says issuers can avoid having interest on their bonds declared taxable by paying the Treasury Dept. the difference between the price they paid and the spot price of the securities on the purchase date, plus interest.

The groups, including the National League of Cities and U.S. Conference of Mayors, said the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, enacted by the 104th Congress, requires federal agencies to prepare written analyses of any mandate that is likely to cost the public or private sector at least $100 million.

"The kinds of documentation required by this regulation, in terms of staff time and resources spent by state and local governments and the private sector, could easily exceed the $100 million threshold if applied to all issuers in the universe of financings," the group said.

Also signing the letter, addressed to Donald Lubick, Treasury's assistant secretary for tax policy, are the National Governors' Association, International City/County Management Association, National Association of Counties, Council of State Governments and the National Conference of State Legislatures.
